date_note: Mailed July 31, 1969 in three parts of 8 rows each: part 1 (rows 0-7) to the Vallejo Times-Herald, part 2 (rows 8-15) to the San Francisco Examiner, part 3 (rows 16-23) to the San Francisco Chronicle. Solved by Donald and Bettye Harden; their solution reached the Chronicle on August 8, 1969.

plaintext_note: Letters only, 1:1 with ascii, as the Hardens' worksheet reads it (Oranchak's annotated solution): Zodiac's own misspellings are kept (Oranchak notes 6, 10, 14) and the last 18 letters (positions 390-407) are the Hardens'/community reading of the unexplained tail. At the 8 positions in encoding_slips the letter is the intended one, not the key's. Popular renderings (e.g. Wikipedia) keep the key letter at 107 and 110 instead, which produces two well-known 'misspellings'. plaintext_key_decoded is the strict one-letter-per-symbol reading.

encoding_slips.explanation: Oranchak note 7: the solid triangle '8' stands for A 4x, S 3x and I 1x; S is otherwise '7' or another S homophone and I is otherwise the open triangle '9', so Zodiac apparently confused his own triangle symbols.
Oranchak notes 8 and 20: the word should end in S but the symbol is 'E' (key E); the S homophone 'F' looks similar. With '!' at 105 (note 20) only this last symbol is wrong.

Oranchak note 7: the solid triangle '8' stands for A 4x, S 3x and I 1x; S is otherwise '7' or another S homophone and I is otherwise the open triangle '9', so Zodiac apparently confused his own triangle symbols.

Oranchak note 7: the solid triangle '8' stands for A 4x, S 3x and I 1x; S is otherwise '7' or another S homophone and I is otherwise the open triangle '9', so Zodiac apparently confused his own triangle symbols.
Oranchak note 13: 'N' stands for E 5x and T 1x; Zodiac probably wrote 'N' where he meant the T homophone 'H'.
Oranchak note 15: the dotted triangle '7' stands for S 2x and A 1x; A is otherwise the solid triangle '8' (triangle confusion again).
Oranchak note 18: the open triangle '9' stands for I 13x and W 1x; W is otherwise 'A' (triangle-shaped symbols again).

transcription_variants.note: Oranchak's annotated key note 20: long read as a plain I (as the Hardens did, and as AZdecrypt's file still has it), but on closer inspection it is the 'funny I' (key O). With 'I' the key reads T there.

key_variants.note: '7' stands for S at 41 and 352 and for A at 264 in the Hardens' plaintext. The majority letter S is used here (as in Oranchak's visualizer); AZdecrypt's solved file uses A.

unsolved_tail.note: The last 18 symbols decode under the key to a string with no accepted reading (Oranchak note 19; arXiv:2403.17350 section 8.2.2, where they are called Z18). The 18 positions use 15 distinct symbols (12 of them once), all of which also occur in the first 390. Hypotheses: filler to square off part 3, possibly copied from symbols above (Brax Sisco 2009), or a second hidden message.

notes: ASCII convention: Oranchak / AZdecrypt / Cipher Explorer. Upper-case letters are normal letters, lower-case letters are mirror-reversed letters, except z (Zodiac crosshair) and t (upside-down T); digits and punctuation are shapes (see symbols[].description). Same convention as z13.json, z32.json and z340.json.

Verification (tools/verify_calibration.js): applying key to ascii reproduces plaintext except at the 8 encoding_slips positions (97, 107, 110, 146, 228, 232, 264, 345); it reproduces plaintext_key_decoded and Oranchak's z408-pt.txt exactly; the key equals the majority reading of the Harden key table on Oranchak's page.
A word appears to be missing at the part 2 / part 3 boundary (position 272; Oranchak note 16). This is not a position mismatch and is not represented in the plaintext.
Harden worksheet slips that are not Zodiac's (Oranchak notes 1, 2, 4, 9, 11, 17) are already corrected in the plaintext.
